title: Gemini now lets you edit Docs and PDFs inside the chat
description: Google Gemini can now create and edit Docs, Sheets, slides and PDFs right in the chat. Here's what that means for small business owners and how to try it.

blocks.text: Google has made Gemini a lot more useful for everyday office work. You can now generate, preview and edit files directly inside a Gemini chat, including PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, plain text files and code. No more copying output into another app just to fix a heading.

According to [The Verge's report on the update](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1022519/google-gemini-file-editing-documents-pdfs), it's rolling out to all Gemini users. There's one catch. PDF previews and edits work on both web and mobile, but every other file type is web only for now.
Earlier this year Google let Gemini create files you could download. Useful, but clunky. If the draft was 90% right, you still had to open it somewhere else to fix the last 10%.

Now you can expand a file to full screen and work on it right there. The clever part is highlighting. Select a paragraph, a list or a table, then ask Gemini a question about it or tell it what to change. Google's own example is highlighting a table and asking Gemini to turn it into a graph.

That's a small interface change with a big effect on how it feels. Instead of rewriting a whole prompt and getting a whole new document back, you point at the bit that's wrong and fix just that. It's closer to working with a colleague than a vending machine.
Why this matters for a small business

Picture a two-person real-estate team in Dubai. They need a one-page property summary, a simple price comparison sheet and a short slide deck for a landlord meeting. Before, that meant Gemini for the draft, then Docs, Sheets and Slides for the tidy-up. Now the whole loop can happen in one window.

Or a dental clinic in Dubai Marina that wants a patient aftercare PDF. Draft it, highlight the section that sounds too clinical, ask for friendlier wording, and you're done. Less switching, fewer lost versions, less time staring at three browser tabs.

To be fair, this isn't brand new territory. You could already use Gemini inside Google's Workspace apps, like the Gemini bar in Google Docs. And Anthropic added something similar to Claude earlier this year, letting people create and edit documents and presentations in the chat. What's changed is that Gemini users now get it in the main app, not just as a sidebar in each tool.
A few things worth trying this week

items: Ask Gemini for a one-page price list or service menu as a Google Doc, then highlight any line that sounds stiff and ask it to rewrite just that part.
Paste last month's sales or booking numbers, ask for a Google Sheet, then highlight the table and ask for a graph you can drop into a team update.
Have it draft a five-slide deck for a supplier or landlord meeting, and refine slide by slide instead of starting over.
Upload a PDF you send to customers, like a welcome pack or aftercare sheet, and ask it to tighten the wording. This one works on your phone too.
Keep the final check human. Read every number, price and policy line yourself before anything goes out.

blocks.text: Faster editing doesn't make the content more accurate. Gemini can still get facts wrong or invent details, and a nicely formatted document makes mistakes look more believable, not less. Treat it as a quick first draft and an editing helper, not the final word.
The mobile limit matters too. If you do most of your admin on a phone between appointments, only PDFs get the new treatment for now. For Docs, Sheets and slides, you'll want to sit down at a laptop.

And if you're producing the same kinds of documents every week, like listings, newsletters or blog posts, a chat window is still a manual process. That's the point where it's worth setting up proper [AI content automation](https://www.f21studio.com/services/ai-content-automation) so the routine stuff happens without you prompting it every time.

Our honest take: this is one of those updates that won't make headlines for long but will quietly save you twenty minutes here and there. Pick one boring document you dread making, try building it start to finish inside Gemini, and see how it feels. If it sticks, you've got a new habit. If it doesn't, you've lost a coffee break.

takeaways: Gemini can now generate, preview and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Sheets, slide decks, Markdown, TXT files and code without you leaving the chat.
It's available to all Gemini users, but only PDFs work on mobile for now, and every other format is web only.
The most useful trick is highlighting part of a file and asking Gemini to change it, like turning a table into a graph.

faq.q: Can I edit Google Docs inside Gemini on my phone?
faq.a: Not yet. On mobile, only PDF previews and editing are supported right now. Google Docs, Sheets, slides and other formats need the web version of Gemini.
The feature is available to all Gemini users, according to The Verge. The report doesn't separate free and paid plans, so check your own account to see what you have.

faq.q: Which file types can Gemini create and edit?
faq.a: Gemini can generate, preview and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files and code. You can also highlight part of a file and ask Gemini to change it.
